questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and that the culture were supposed to be diffrent than the kultures I already know. Also that it were a place with adventure opportunitet.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The website for the university of Akureyri were pretty easy to navigate, but it were a little difficult to know how much I should do or if I missed something on an external website like OLA (online learning agreement). But my home university coordinaters were pretty fast to answere on mail if I had any questions, so my recomedations is just to reach out to them if you got any questions.
I had an extra half year of waiting without doing anything cause I went on exchange in the spring semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The hosty university had a introduction day before the weekend, to welcome the excange students, and explain everything about the university, and how it works diffrently than other universities. 
The host universities exchange coordianters were also kind to reach out to me, cause I were intrested in courses on one of their university collaborations (university center of the westfjords). So she let me know it weren't possibel for them to share courses and that I could chooses either, then she would forward me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
They were pretty good at taking us in, and the univeristy of Akureyri celebrates their exchange students, cause the icelandic students are mostly studing remote. 
I also recived help in relation to extrendet time for the exames cause I'm dyslectic, and it were so easy I just sended my documentation to their admistrative office, and they ensured that it were sat up in all my exames.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Our host university have a collaborations with something called FESTA, which are respolsibel for student recommedation all ower the city. and they had pretty many spots, and if there wouldn't be enought the uniersity would assist FESTA in getting new student housing arrangements. 

They have different appartmens all showen on their website, I recomend that you write you wishes for an appartment in your "Statement of objectives and expectations". Also if you wish to share an appartment with someone special, or to have a common Kitchen or something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Be prepaird to walk slow and carefully in the wintertimes, there will be a lot of snow and specially ice. The city is small enough to walke all over the city, it take max 30 min. and if you are up for keeping time on the busses (which leave once an hour) then they are free in Akureyri. 
You can also look on facebook marketplace for a bike, og see if you can borrow one though connections in the city. 

There is a pretty walking rout fare from busy roads when living at Ùtstein

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The houses were fine, and my room were big. But if there were something not working FESTA didn't always come an cheek it, it were like they only had their attention on the buildings in the move out period. Some of the other exchange students experienced thaty if something with greater difficulties didn't woirk, they it didn't get fixed. But we were missing some pans in the common kitchens, and they provided theses the day after we notified them about it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You start with choosing the wished courses but as they write clear it is not sure that all the courses will be runned, which you first know after the introduction day, and open you knew study email connected to your host university. 
But after the beginign you have 2 weeks to change courses, and/or try out other coruses. it is better to sign up to courses and then later drop out before the exames than having to few courses. 
The professors keep on going with their cours the first two weeks even though new peopel are joining. Some courses are really intense in the beginning of the semester and ends fast and others begin later in the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: And the exchange coordinators are very sweet at helping you registering with to the right once, or help you find a course closer to one of the canceld once. You can choose both graduate and undergraduate.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended with three out of five of my original choosen courses, cause one got canceled due to few registred and I choosed anotherone cause the professor were better after talking with the other exchange students about there expereinces of the course the first week.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Here what the other exchange students think about there courses, and maybe change if it sounds better. Also sigh up to more courses than need just to try them out to finde some that fit you and your profile.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it came as quite a shook for all the exchange students that it were a remote stuies university, but this actually ended up as an advantage, couse you had better and more communication with your professors, you could go on roadtrips in the weekdays and not miss any lectures.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one master course and 4 BA courses, you could feel a clear diffrence in the workload in the MA course. But my MA course were also a part of the univeristys PolarLaw program, which in genneral has a greater workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The academic level were easier, but I'm not sure if this were just because I wasn't following my regular program. The final grade were mainly divided into multipel parts, which were a great advantage, so you could devide you energy better doing the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The undergraguate courses: 
VKS1206140 Project Management 
INJFU06030 Icelandic nature
ÞMN0276110 Peoples and Cultures of the Circumpolar North
FSÁ0176110 Social Psychology

The Mastercourse: 
GNR1076210 Governance of Natural Resources at the Poles

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The course Icelandic nature were a really good introduction to Iceland, which were really nice when traveling around, also for understanding some of the processes going on in the landscape.  and to get familar with the animals. 

I also really recomend the course "Peoples and Cultures of the Circumpolar North" cause it gives a good perspective on the north and indigenous nordic development, which is often forgotten.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I brought a youth (15-25) year seasonal pass for the local swimminpool, which is really recommended, it costed 1055 DKK. 
I also brought a seasonal skiing pass for 1600DKK Which I also were really happy for.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The alcohol were really expensive, same with some vegstabels. You relly have to look oiut for some items are crasy expensive and others can exchange thoughse so just keep an eye out for that. 

i lived without missing anyhthing, and were eating out some times, this is reflected in my personal spendings. So it is perfectly possibel to live cheeper than I did.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The universty had a GYM which were open if you get a smartkey from the university. This were really used by a lot of the exchange students and really a nice add. So you could study all day at there luxurious libary and then take a gym break. 

They also have a student union, which were having some activities. Where you as exchange student sign up to the union fitting your studies the best.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really rocomend the swimminpool, as a meetup place, either just for chilling, fun or swimming exercises. It is a local oasis even in the wintertimes. 

I also recommend practise some skiing, I were happy to learn how to snowboard on there hill, by borrowing a snowboard and shoes, or you can by some cheep used once in hartex or facebook marketplace. 

Otherrwise I know a lot from our exchange team signed up for local sports teams like volleyball or boxing, which they where happy for.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
i really recomend renting a car and going on roadtrips around the country, there is great natural diffrences allwoer the island, and to have so long time there, is a uniq possibility to experience all it's sites. 
My personal favorites are the arctic henges in the north east and a puffin island in the east corner "Borgarfjarðarhöfn". 

you can also go on skiing adventures if you befriend the peopel at the ski renting place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Peopel living in Iceland are quite simmilar to Danes, they might just be a littel more afraid of breaking codex. But to ajust to the cold and darkness of the winter were a great challange, and the same with the light in the summer, so bring a sleepingmask and Vitamin D. But they also have a great amount of vitamin supliment produkts so don't worry.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be prepaird to break the ice and just be the one to inisiate conversation, break a littel out of the exhange group and go to some event only for icelanders, they you'll for sure make some lokal freinds. Which I also really recommend, to have local friends really enhances you ecperience of the culture. Plus they are really sweet. 
As a dane I expereinced a lot of Icelanders above 40 who wanted to practise some Danish, but don't expect it from the youth.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
A greater shyness of sticking out of the social norms. But this is only untill they feel comfortable with you. 
It is also quite a challenge driving in the fog which just apperes and with snowy reoads, but you'll manage if you just drive carefully, and don't go anywhere maked as closed. ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There kindness and willingness to help wherever they can. This must be in there culture. They have a saing meaning somthing related to "don't worry, it will all turn out alright"

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress to much about the courses. The exchange is what you make it, so if you want great expereinces be sure to create them and put yourself out there. 
Take you vitamin D, and host some good paties yourself. 
But be awair the snow and the winds kills, if you are not protected, so don't fool around careless.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you don't fit in with thoughs you live with, just hang out with some other peopel.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The expereinces I had, and the freinds I made, your attitude shapes you expereince.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving everything back home, so be sure to make it worth it, and remember noone but you knows what is woth it. Enjoy the precent even though you'll never feel completly ready for and expereince like this.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
